drivingQuestion: With what substances may the blood of slaughter be covered, and with what may it not?
outcomeNote: A mishna: an enumerated ruling followed by Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's general criterion; nothing is argued out here.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ בַּמֶּה מְכַסִּין וּבַמֶּה אֵין מְכַסִּין? מְכַסִּין בְּזֶבֶל הַדַּק, וּבְחוֹל הַדַּק, בְּסִיד, וּבְחַרְסִית, וּבִלְבֵנָה וּבִמְגוּפָה שֶׁכְּתָשָׁן, אֲבָל אֵין מְכַסִּין לֹא בְּזֶבֶל הַגַּס, וְלֹא בְּחוֹל הַגַּס, וְלֹא בִּלְבֵנָה וּבִמְגוּפָה שֶׁלֹּא כְּתָשָׁן, וְלֹא יִכְפֶּה עָלָיו אֶת הַכְּלִי. כְּלָל אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: דָּבָר שֶׁמְּגַדֵּל בּוֹ צְמָחִים – מְכַסִּין בּוֹ, וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְגַדֵּל צְמָחִים – אֵין מְכַסִּין בּוֹ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «With what» substances «may one cover» the blood «and with what» substances «may one not cover» the blood? «One» may «cover» the blood «with fine» granulated «manure, with fine sand, with lime, with» crushed «potsherd, and with a brick or» the «lid» of an earthenware barrel «that one crushed. But one may not cover» the blood «with thick manure, nor with thick,» clumped «sand, nor with a brick or the lid» of an earthenware barrel «that one did not crush. Neither may one» merely «turn a vessel over» the blood. «Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel stated a principle:» With regard to «a substance in which plants grow, one may cover» blood «with it; and» with regard to a substance in «which plants do not grow, one may not cover» blood «with it.»

moves.summary: The mishna poses its own topic and enumerates the substances valid and invalid for covering the blood, adding that one may not merely invert a vessel over it.
moves.about: what the governing criterion is behind the mishna's list of substances valid for covering the blood — Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel replaces the enumeration with the single test of whether plants grow in the substance

moves.cueHe: כלל אמר רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
moves.summary: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel states the governing principle: whatever grows plants may be used, whatever does not may not.
